boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Old Fort Wayne record (October 22, 1862) in Operations North of Boston Mountains [August-November 1862]. Blunt's night march of October 21-22 and the pursuit to Spavina Creek are context; Cooper's December 15 report also narrates the October 4 evacuation of Newtonia, which is not part of this record. The live NPS campaign label ("Confederate Offensive North of Boston Mountains") does not replace the frozen campaign. Campaign-wide totals, marches and multi-action loss figures are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names Blunt's 1st Division, Army of the Frontier against the 1st Brigade without counts; the live field reads zero. Blunt's dispatch estimates the enemy at 4,000 to 7,000; his report gives 5,000 to 7,000 from scouts and near 7,000 from a local informant who said two Texas regiments had just joined, and says the Second Kansas with less than 600 men engaged a force more than ten times its number. Cooper says Rains had taken his four Texas regiments, that the Federal strength was at least 5,000 against his about 1,500, and at least three times his.
claims.rationale: Detachment and brigade estimates on the same day, with a direct conflict over the Texas regiments' presence. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Blunt says he went ahead disguised as an escaped rebel and learned the pickets, camp and strength from a woman whose husband was in the Confederate camp; the pickets heard his approach and alarmed the town, and he found that only three companies had kept up with him. Cooper says he learned on the evening of the 21st of a Federal force moving from Bentonville but took it for a scout, and that the Federals had been informed of his position by persons about his camps.
claims.rationale: Reported knowledge in opposing interested reports; no message chain inspected.

claims.value: The frozen rows list Cooper (Colonel) and Blunt (Brigadier General); the live page styles Cooper Brigadier General, and his December report is signed as Brigadier-General. Blunt led the advance, opened with the Second Kansas and two howitzers, and credits Crawford's charge with taking the battery; he blames the main column's failure to move as ordered for the lost surprise. Cooper says he was ill and that Lieutenant-Colonel Buster was in command on the day of the battle, and that Watie had command during his illness when he wrote on October 25; he blames Rains's detachment of the Texas regiments, Sampson Folsom's disobedience and his own illness.
claims.rationale: The listed Confederate commander was, by his own account, not directing the fight; Buster and Watie are not listed commanders. No listed commander receives automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live results are Union victory. Blunt reports the complete rout of the enemy with the loss of all his artillery and a flight to Fort Gibson, 70 miles. Cooper says that but for the loss of the battery his troops would have had the advantage and the Federals had nothing to pride themselves on. NPS says overwhelming numbers forced the Confederates off the field after half an hour.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: Frozen and live: 164 total (US 14; CS 150). Blunt's dispatch gives 4 killed and about 15 wounded and 30 prisoners; his report gives 1 killed and 9 wounded, 4 of them mortally, about 50 Confederate dead buried, and 150 killed and wounded reported by Confederate wounded found in houses. Cooper gives 6 killed and about 30 wounded, and the Federal loss as 75 to 100. The compiled Confederate return's total line is garbled in OCR.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The frozen CS 150 equals the figure Blunt attributes to Confederate wounded in houses; that is an observation, not a reconciliation.
